rationale: Provides a security scanning pipeline to evaluate vulnerabilities, malicious patterns, and safety risks in AI agent tools and skills prior to execution.
Provides an automated red teaming framework to evaluate safety risks, vulnerabilities, and adversarial attack vectors in LLM-based agent systems.
Provides the ADR-Bench benchmark containing over 300 enterprise tasks and 133 MCP servers to evaluate safety risks and attack vulnerabilities in AI agents.
Implements runtime agentic detection and response to monitor intent and detect risky agent behaviors and tool executions at inference time.
Provides an open-source text metrics toolkit to extract real-time safety signals, detecting prompt injection, toxic content, and sensitive patterns during inference.
Implements an inference-time security scanner to detect prompt injections, jailbreaks, and risky inputs and responses using YARA heuristics and vector similarity.
Provides a standardized evaluation framework to assess and benchmark LLM refusal and vulnerability to jailbreaks involving severe and harmful behaviors.
Enables behavioral regression and capability evaluation for AI agents through snapshot testing of tool-calling trajectories and responses.
Provides an ultra-fast inference-time filtering library to scrutinize prompts and detect prompt injection attacks, jailbreaks, and exploits before model execution.
Provides a comprehensive red-teaming benchmark dataset and evaluation suite to assess language model safety across multiple severe and catastrophic risk categories.
Implements a unified, optimized evaluation orchestration engine supporting distributed execution and inference acceleration to run evaluation suites efficiently.
Provides a security auditing and evaluation tool to assess prompt injection vulnerabilities, token leaks, and tool poisoning risks in Model Context Protocol (MCP) agent environments.
